q1: SELECT C.NAME FROM CARRIERS AS C JOIN FLIGHTS AS F ON C.CID = F.CARRIER_ID GROUP BY C.CID, C.NAME, F.YEAR, F.MONTH_ID, F.DAY_OF_MONTH HAVING COUNT(F.FID) > 1000
q2: SELECT C.NAME FROM CARRIERS AS C JOIN FLIGHTS AS F ON C.CID = F.CARRIER_ID GROUP BY C.NAME, F.DAY_OF_MONTH HAVING COUNT(F.FID) > 1000

counterexample: INSERT INTO CARRIERS (CID, NAME) VALUES (1, 'AA'), (2, 'AA'); INSERT INTO FLIGHTS (FID, YEAR, MONTH_ID, DAY_OF_MONTH, CARRIER_ID) VALUES (1, 2020, 1, 1, 1), (2, 2020, 1, 1, 2), (3, 2021, 1, 1, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they group by different sets of columns. Q1 groups by C.CID, C.NAME, F.YEAR, F.MONTH_ID, F.DAY_OF_MONTH, while Q2 groups by C.NAME, F.DAY_OF_MONTH. This difference in grouping can lead to different results, especially if there are multiple carriers with the same name operating flights on the same day of the month in different years or months.
